sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, password_hash, role, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: email: unique — POST /auth/login resolves the caller via findByEmail; must be a fast, unique lookup; employee_number: unique — existing findByEmployeeNumber lookup; manager_id: MANAGER role scoping for GET /leaves uses findByManagerId (direct reports); currently unindexed and must be added

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_code, start_date, end_date, requested_days, reason, status, approver_id, approval_comment, submitted_at, decided_at, cancelled_by, cancelled_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_code -> leave_types.code; approver_id -> employees.id; cancelled_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: role scoping for GET /leaves and GET /leaves/:id filters by employee_id (self or direct reports); status: status filter on GET /leaves; (employee_id, status): composite — the dominant list query scopes by employee then filters by status; (leave_type_code, start_date): date-range + type filtering on GET /leaves

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_code, period_start, period_end, entitled_days, used_days, pending_days | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_code -> leave_types.code | indexes: (employee_id, leave_type_code, period_start, period_end): unique — findByKey lookup for GET /balances/me and balance resolution; employee_id: balance lookups by employee

table leave_policies | fields: id, leave_type_code, policy_name, annual_entitlement_days, accrual_period_months, carry_forward_days, min_notice_days, max_request_days, requires_manager_approval, effective_from, effective_to, status | pk: id | fks: leave_type_code -> leave_types.code | indexes: leave_type_code: findAll() is filtered per leaveTypeCode for GET /balances/me (ACTIVE + effective window, latest effective_from)

methods: findByQuery(params, client?) — extended to honour params.employeeIds via employee_id = ANY($n)
findAll(client?) — unfiltered; the new IPolicyService method filters ACTIVE/effective and dedupes per leaveTypeCode
findByKey(employeeId, leaveTypeCode, periodStart, periodEnd, client?, forUpdate?)
getActivePolicies(asOf) — NEW: findAll() filtered to ACTIVE + effective window, at most one per leaveTypeCode (latest effective_from)
repositories.backing: PostgreSQL via pg Pool (via IPolicyRepository / PgLeavePolicyRepository)

data_notes:
Persistence changes are minimal and additive. The only schema change is a nullable `password_hash` column on `employees` (text contract, per the initial-schema convention of `t.text(...)` for text-contract columns). No new tables are introduced — the feature reuses employees, leave_requests, leave_balances, and leave_policies.

Repository changes:
- IEmployeeRepository gains `findByManagerId(managerId)` (PgEmployeeRepository) for MANAGER role scoping (direct reports). `findByEmail` already exists and serves POST /auth/login.
- ILeaveRepository.findByQuery is extended to honour a new `employeeIds?: string[]` on LeaveRequestQueryParams, matched with `employee_id = ANY($n)` — role scoping stays in the query, never in application code.
- IPolicyService gains `getActivePolicies(asOf)` (PolicyService) which calls the existing `IPolicyRepository.findAll()` and filters to ACTIVE + effective window, returning at most one policy per leaveTypeCode (latest effective_from). No new repository method; balance depends on policy's own factory (createPolicyService), never hand-wires policy internals.

Index rationale additions: `employees.manager_id` (currently unindexed) must be indexed for findByManagerId; `leave_requests.employee_id` is covered by the existing (employee_id, status) composite but the single-column employee_id index is noted for the id-scoped GET /leaves/:id visibility check.

Read endpoints are read-only and open no transaction; POST /auth/login is a single read (bcrypt compare + signToken) with no multi-step write. No transaction contract is required.
transaction_contract: EMPTY — this feature is read-only plus a single-read login (bcrypt compare + token mint). No multi-step writes exist, so no unit-of-work contract is introduced. Existing write endpoints and their PgUnitOfWork semantics are unchanged.
